content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What the document says**
- **§4.1 (p0024):** one-year term, auto-renewing annually, terminable by *either* Party on 90 days' written notice. The notice mechanics sit at the playbook fallback (Customer 60–90 days; HDI's symmetric right effectively bites at the renewal date), so I did not redline them.
- **§4.2(a) (p0026):** if *the Company* terminates, it owes a "Termination Payment" of (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2, payable in eight quarterly instalments (p0029). HDI owes nothing on its own exit (p0028).

**Why it fails the fallback**
Our fees are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month (§3.1). The Termination Payment is 50% of Net Sales above $800,000 — at $2M of annual Net Sales that is roughly $600k against ~$140k of three months' fees. The fallback tolerates an early-termination fee of no more than 3 months' fees; this uncapped, one-sided formula is a penalty on our convenience exit and materially breaches it.

**Redline (validated, ok:true)**
Minimal proviso added to §4.2(a) capping the Termination Payment at three months' §3.1 fees, and disapplying it entirely where we terminate for HDI's breach or under the §1.6 launch-failure right. I pitched at the fallback rather than preferred (no fee) because HDI is compensated purely by revenue share with no upfront fee — a zero-fee exit would be disproportionate to that bargain. Note also that no pro-rata refund language is needed: fees are paid monthly in arrears, so there are no prepaid fees.
